reforms.description: The SBA created the Angel Capital Electronic Network (ACE-Net), a nation-wide Internet listing of small innovative companies with restricted access to angels, and coordinated with State Securities Administrators to remove inter-state trading restrictions on unregistered stocks of ACE-Net companies.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Reduces information asymmetries and regulatory barriers in angel capital markets, improving capital allocation to innovative startups and supporting entrepreneurial growth.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'the SBA has taken the initiative to create the Angel Capital Electronic Network (ACE-Net)' and describes it as operational with State Securities Administrators having agreed to remove restrictions.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant initiative addressing a structural gap in startup financing by creating a nation-wide platform and removing inter-state regulatory barriers, with meaningful implications for angel capital market development.
reforms.source_quote: In these circumstances, the SBA has taken the initiative to create the Angel Capital Electronic Network (ACE-Net). This is a nation-wide Internet listing of small innovative companies with the access restricted to angels.

reforms.description: The Advanced Technology Program (ATP) provides funding to assist US businesses to apply or commercialise new scientific discoveries, with the goal of increasing high-risk research and forging stronger links between the research community and enterprise.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Supports commercialisation of scientific discoveries and increases high-risk research, bridging the gap between research and enterprise to accelerate innovation-driven growth.
reforms.status_evidence: Text describes ATP as an existing programme that has been evaluated, indicating it is operational.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant direct support instrument for private-sector innovation and commercialisation, though evaluation results were disputed and impact remains uncertain.
reforms.source_quote: ATP provides funding to assist US businesses to apply or commercialise new scientific discoveries. A Department of Commerce evaluation found that the ATP increased high-risk research, implying that stronger links were being forged between the research community and enterprise.

reforms.description: The Manufacturing Extension Partnership (MEP) is a nation-wide network of locally managed manufacturing extension centres dedicated to helping smaller manufacturers improve competitiveness by adopting modern technologies, initially designed to transfer advanced technologies from government research institutes.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Facilitates technology transfer and adoption of modern technologies among small manufacturers, improving productivity and competitiveness, though awareness and uptake barriers limit impact.
reforms.status_evidence: Text describes MEP as an established nation-wide network with operational centres and survey data on user satisfaction, indicating it is in operation.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant nation-wide technology transfer and diffusion programme with demonstrated positive effects on user firms, though limited awareness constrains overall impact.
reforms.source_quote: MEP is a nation-wide network of locally managed manufacturing extension centres dedicated to helping smaller manufacturers improve their competitiveness by adopting modern technologies.

reforms.description: Science parks were promoted by sub-national US governments during the 1980s as a strategy to support technological development and create high-tech jobs. These parks feature industry-driven R&D activities, links with research facilities (universities or institutes), and are supported through infrastructure provision, tax breaks, and fiscal incentives.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Science parks can generate economic development and high job creation when successful, but high failure rates (approximately 50% of parks closed) and reliance on attracting external firms rather than generating spinoffs create significant inefficiencies and uncertain returns on public investment.
reforms.status_evidence: During the 1980s, many sub-national governments looked to technological development to revive their local economies and create jobs through the creation of science parks.
reforms.importance_rationale: Science parks represent a significant sub-national innovation policy initiative spanning multiple states, with substantial public investment in infrastructure and fiscal incentives. However, the assessment notes high failure rates and limited evidence of effectiveness, suggesting mixed systemic impact despite broad geographic reach.
reforms.source_quote: Science parks are a type of business park where the primary activity of the majority of the establishments is industry-driven R&D. State and local authorities support science parks through the provision of infrastructure and land, tax breaks and tax holidays, promotion – primarily through marketing campaigns and lobbying – and other fiscal and physical incentives.
